hero.subtitle: When a diagnosis, surgery, or hospital stay goes wrong in Galt, the aftermath can feel isolating. We understand California's medical malpractice rules and can review what happened to determine whether you have a case.

about.title: Galt Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Galt residents rely on a mix of local clinics and Sacramento County hospitals for care, and most visits go the way they should. But when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mismanages medication, the consequences can follow a patient for years. California law treats these cases differently than a typical injury claim — there are strict notice requirements, tight filing deadlines, and a legal standard that requires proof the care fell below what a reasonably careful provider would have done. A disappointing result on its own isn't enough; the law asks whether the provider deviated from accepted medical practice. If you or a family member were harmed by care received in or near Galt, we handle these claims and can help you understand whether you have a case worth pursuing, at no upfront cost.

items.title: Strict Deadlines Are Tracked Carefully
items.desc: California generally gives one year from when the harm was discovered, and no more than three years from the injury itself, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice. We help make sure none of these deadlines slip by.

items.title: Expert Review Is Built Into the Process
items.desc: California nearly always requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in on whether the care given fell short. We work with the right kind of medical review to evaluate your claim properly.

items.title: Understanding the Non-Economic Damages Cap
items.desc: State law places a cap on non-economic damages that rises each year, which can shape how a claim is valued. We can explain how this applies to your specific circumstances.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery near Galt — does that automatically mean malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law requires showing that a provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, not just that the result was disappointing. We can review your medical records to determine whether the treatment you received in the Galt area met that standard.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date of the injury itself. There's also a required 90-day notice period before a lawsuit can be filed, so timing matters early on. We can help calculate your specific deadlines.

items.question: Do I need to travel outside Galt to find a malpractice attorney?
items.answer: No. We handle medical malpractice cases arising from care received locally or at nearby Sacramento County facilities. The consultation is free and there's no obligation to move forward.
